Blank-correct OD

blank_correct.Rd

Subtracts a blank from every read and clips the result at zero (negative OD is not allowed). The original od is kept. Two ways to define the blank:

Usage

blank_correct(
  data,
  blank = NULL,
  n_reads = 5,
  od = "od",
  smooth = FALSE,
  window = 5
)

Arguments

data

Tidy data frame from one of the readers.

blank

NULL to use each well's initial reads, or the blank well(s). Give a data frame with columns plate_id and well, or, when data has no plate_id column, a character vector of well ids.

n_reads

Number of initial reads averaged when blank = NULL.

od

Name of the OD column.

smooth

If TRUE, also add a rolling-mean-smoothed copy of the corrected OD with smooth_od(). Off by default.

window

Window size for smoothing; see smooth_od().

Value

data with added columns blank_od (the value subtracted at that row) and od_corrected (od - blank_od, never below zero), plus od_corrected_rollmean if smooth = TRUE.

Details

  • Blank wells (blank supplied): the blank is the OD of the specified well(s), matched by time point within the same plate. If several blank wells are given for a plate their ODs are averaged at each time point. Every well on a plate is corrected using the blank well(s) of that plate, so each plate in data needs at least one blank well. Times must line up between wells, which the readers ensure by snapping times (see snap_hours()).

  • Initial reads (blank = NULL): each well is corrected by the mean of its own first n_reads reads.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "bioscreen_example.txt", package = "plateReadeR")
d <- read_bioscreen(f)
# each well minus the mean of its first 5 reads
blank_correct(d)
#> # A tibble: 4,000 × 8
#>    seconds  hours plate_id well  well_index    od blank_od od_corrected
#>      <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>    <chr>      <int> <dbl>    <dbl>        <dbl>
#>  1       0 0      Plate 1  001            1 0.072    0.072      0      
#>  2     300 0.0833 Plate 1  001            1 0.072    0.072      0      
#>  3     600 0.167  Plate 1  001            1 0.072    0.072      0      
#>  4     900 0.25   Plate 1  001            1 0.072    0.072      0      
#>  5    1200 0.333  Plate 1  001            1 0.072    0.072      0      
#>  6    1500 0.417  Plate 1  001            1 0.072    0.072      0      
#>  7    1800 0.5    Plate 1  001            1 0.072    0.072      0      
#>  8    2100 0.583  Plate 1  001            1 0.072    0.072      0      
#>  9    2400 0.667  Plate 1  001            1 0.072    0.072      0      
#> 10    2700 0.75   Plate 1  001            1 0.073    0.072      0.00100
#> # ℹ 3,990 more rows
# wells 001 and 002 on each plate are blanks
blanks <- data.frame(
  plate_id = rep(c("Plate 1", "Plate 2"), each = 2),
  well = c("001", "002", "001", "002")
)
blank_correct(d, blank = blanks)
#> # A tibble: 4,000 × 8
#>    seconds  hours plate_id well  well_index    od blank_od od_corrected
#>      <dbl>  <dbl> <chr>    <chr>      <int> <dbl>    <dbl>        <dbl>

#>  3     600 0.167  Plate 1  001            1 0.072   0.072      0       
#>  4     900 0.25   Plate 1  001            1 0.072   0.0715     0.000500
